name: The prophets of Baal at Carmel
charge: Prophesying in the name of Baal and eating at Jezebel’s table; crying from morning to noon to a god that could not answer
summary: The four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal, with the four hundred prophets of the groves, ate at Jezebel’s table, and Elijah called them to Mount Carmel before all Israel (1 Kings 18:19-24). They dressed their bullock and cried to Baal from morning until past noon, leaped on their altar and cut themselves till the blood gushed out, but no one answered (1 Kings 18:25-29). When Elijah prayed, the fire of the Lord fell, the people confessed that the Lord is God, and the prophets of Baal were taken down to the brook Kishon and slain (1 Kings 18:36-40).
offenseFull: Elijah told Ahab to gather all Israel to Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves who ate at Jezebel’s table (1 Kings 18:19). The study notes say Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her. The Revelation 2 teaching on Thyatira adds that these prophets were men, weak men under the authority of an evil woman, taking orders from her and eating at her table, while she killed the real prophets of God. Walking in Elijah’s Footsteps calls Baal what he is: the devil.

Elijah asked the people how long they would halt between two opinions: if the Lord is God, follow Him; if Baal, follow him. The people answered not a word (1 Kings 18:21). He said he alone remained a prophet of the Lord against four hundred and fifty, and proposed the test: each side would lay a bullock on wood with no fire under it, and the God who answered by fire, let Him be God; the people said it was well spoken (1 Kings 18:22-24). The Mantle class notes that the other nations also sacrificed, but they sacrificed to devils, for God never made a covenant with them.

The prophets of Baal dressed their bullock and called on Baal from morning until noon, crying for him to hear them, but there was no voice and no one answered, and they leaped on the altar they had made (1 Kings 18:25-26). The notes ask the reader to picture it: eight hundred and fifty men running wild while Elijah sat back and watched. At noon Elijah mocked them, telling them to cry louder, for he is a god; perhaps he was talking, or chasing someone, or on a journey, or asleep and must be woken (1 Kings 18:27). They cried aloud and cut themselves with knives and lancets after their manner until the blood gushed out (1 Kings 18:28). Cutting was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal, and it is why the law says no cuttings in the flesh for the dead nor marks printed on the body (Leviticus 19:28); the Mantle class calls it a Hamitic thing that some tribes still practise as tradition. From midday past the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor answer nor anyone who paid attention (1 Kings 18:29). No one answered because the Most High will not give His glory to another nor His praise to graven images (Isaiah 42:8), and all the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens (Psalms 96:4-5). The gods of the nations are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.
judgmentFull: Elijah repaired the altar of the Lord that was broken down with twelve stones for the twelve tribes, for the whole book is about the twelve tribes of Israel. He had the sacrifice drenched three times until the water filled the trench, and at the evening sacrifice he prayed to the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel that the people might know He is God in Israel and that He had turned their heart back again (1 Kings 18:30-37). The fire of the Lord fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench; the people fell on their faces and said the Lord, He is the God (1 Kings 18:38-39).

Elijah told them to take the prophets of Baal and let not one escape, and he brought them down to the brook Kishon and killed them there (1 Kings 18:40). The law had said that the prophet who speaks in the name of other gods shall die (Deuteronomy 18:20). The study notes carry it forward: in the last days it will be the same, and when the Most High rains down fire again by the hand of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape, for those who feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee. Woe to the pastors who destroy and scatter the sheep of His pasture; He will visit on them the evil of their doings (Jeremiah 23:1-2). When Jezebel heard that all her prophets had been slain with the sword, she swore to take Elijah’s life (1 Kings 19:1-2).

lawsResolved.text: A preacher or a prophet who leads people to worship false gods is to be put to death, because he has counseled rebel against God.
Those who entice others to serve pagan gods and religions are to be put to death.
Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.
Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

text.text: Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel’s table.
So Ahab sent unto all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together unto mount Carmel.
And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
Then said Elijah unto the people, I, even I only, remain a prophet of the Lord; but Baal’s prophets are four hundred and fifty men.

Let them therefore give us two bullocks; and let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under: and I will dress the other bullock, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under:
And call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord: and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. And all the people answered and said, It is well spoken.
And Elijah said unto the prophets of Baal, Choose you one bullock for yourselves, and dress it first; for ye are many; and call on the name of your gods, but put no fire under.

And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped upon the altar which was made.

And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.
And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them.
And it came to pass, when midday was past, and they prophesied until the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.

And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy word.
Hear me, O Lord, hear me, that this people may know that thou art the Lord God, and that thou hast turned their heart back again.
Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.
And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God.
And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them: and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slew them there.

For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.

But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.
Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.

Therefore thus saith the Lord God of Israel against the pastors that feed my people; Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the Lord.
And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.
Then Jezebel sent a messenger unto Elijah, saying, So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to morrow about this time.

And Elijah said unto Ahab, Get thee up, eat and drink; for there is a sound of abundance of rain.
So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees,
And said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. And he went up, and looked, and said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times.

And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man’s hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Prepare thy chariot, and get thee down, that the rain stop thee not.
And it came to pass in the mean while, that the heaven was black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel.
